per_question.question: How does NC Medicaid define 'terminally ill' for purposes of hospice eligibility, and what certification is required?
per_question.agent_answer:

Then I’ll answer with the exact definition plus the certification requirements.**NC Medicaid hospice uses the 6-month prognosis standard.** For hospice eligibility, a person is considered **“terminally ill”** when the certifying physician’s clinical judgment is that the individual has **a life expectancy of 6 months or less if the illness runs its normal course**. That wording appears in the federal hospice certification rule that NC Medicaid hospice policy follows. See **42 CFR Part 418, Section 418.22 — “Certification of terminal illness”**: [42 CFR Part 418](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-418).

## What certification is required

### 1) Written certification of terminal illness
NC Medicaid hospice requires the hospice provider to obtain **written certification of terminal illness for each benefit period**. The written certification must generally be obtained **before the hospice submits a claim for payment**. If it cannot be obtained within **2 calendar days after the period begins**, an **oral certification** must be obtained within those 2 days, and the written certification must still be obtained before billing. See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.1 — “Timing of certification”**: [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

### 2) Who must sign the initial certification
For the **initial 90-day period**, NC Medicaid requires a written certification statement from:

- **the hospice medical director or the physician member of the hospice interdisciplinary group (IDG)**; and
- **the individual’s attending physician, if the individual has an attending physician**.

For **subsequent periods**, only certification by **the hospice medical director or the physician member of the hospice IDG** is required. See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.3 — “Sources of certification”**: [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

## What the certification must say/include
Under the federal hospice rule, the certification must:

- specify that the individual’s prognosis is **6 months or less** if the illness runs its normal course;
- be supported by **clinical information and other documentation** in the medical record; and
- include a **brief narrative explanation of the clinical findings** supporting that prognosis.

See **42 CFR Part 418, Section 418.22 — “Certification of terminal illness”**: [42 CFR Part 418](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-418).

NC Medicaid’s hospice policy also says the certification/recertification must include:

- a physician narrative synthesizing the clinical information supporting the terminal diagnosis and attesting the physician composed the narrative after reviewing the clinical information and, where applicable, examining the beneficiary;
- the **election period dates** to which the certification applies; and
- the **signature and date** of the certifying or recertifying physician.

For the **third and later election periods**, the narrative must also explain why the **face-to-face encounter** findings support a life expectancy of six months or less. See **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, unnumbered section “D. Certification and Recertification of Terminal Illness”**: [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment), and **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D, Section 5.4.1 — “Timing of certification”**: [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment).

## Bottom line
For **NC Medicaid hospice**, “terminally ill” means the person has a **prognosis of 6 months or less** if the illness follows its normal course, and hospice must obtain the required **certification of terminal illness** for each benefit period, with the **initial certification** signed by the hospice physician and, if the beneficiary has one, the **attending physician**.

I also checked amendments for **Clinical Coverage Policy 3D** and cited the current authoritative version, effective **March 15, 2024**.

If you want, I can next pull the exact rule on **initial certification vs. later recertifications**, including the **face-to-face requirement** and who may perform it.
